raw_case_text:
A 19-year-old girl presented with swelling in the left side of the neck of 1 year duration. She also had fatigue and headache. She did not have any history of fever or night sweats. Physical examination revealed pallor, icterus, and multiple left cervical lymph nodes. These lymph nodes were firm, nontender, matted, and mobile. Systemic examination showed mild splenomegaly. Laboratory findings on admission were as follows: hemoglobin 3.5 g/dL, total WBC count 4800/mm3(52% neutrophils and 48% lymphocytes), platelet count 225,000/ mm3, MCV 97, MCH 30.5 fL, and reticulocyte 12%. Peripheral smear showed anisopoikilocytosis with macrocytosis and spherocytosis. Bone marrow examination showed erythroid hyperplasia. Biochemical tests were as follows: total bilirubin 3.7 mg/dL, direct bilirubin 2.0 mg/dL, indirect bilirubin 1.7 mg/dL, LDH - 720 U/L and haptoglobulin 20 mg/dL. Coomb's test done prior to transfusion was positive (Table 1 for hematological parameters before starting anti-tuberculosis therapy). Serum levels of urea, creatinine were within normal limits and glucose 6 phosphate dehydrogenase activity was normal. Serologic tests for antinuclear antibodies, human immunodeficiency virus, mycoplasma, hepatitis B and C virus were negative. Left cervical lymph node biopsy showed caseating granulomatous lymphadenitis [Figure 1] Mantoux test was positive (18 mm induration). Chest X-ray was normal and ultrasound of abdomen revealed splenomegaly.
Patient was started on antituberculosis treatment with isoniazid (300 mg qday), rifampicin (450 mg qday), ethambutol (800 mg qday), and pyrazinamide (750 mg bid). Her symptoms of fatigue and headache started improving after 2 weeks of treatment. Hemoglobin improved to 5 gm/dL after 2 weeks of treatment and Coomb's test became negative after 2 months [Table 2]. She is on follow-up and is in excellent health.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 19-year-old female presenting with left neck swelling for one year, accompanied by fatigue and headache.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient presented with a 1-year history of painless, progressive swelling on the left side of her neck. Over the preceding weeks, she developed worsening fatigue and persistent headache. She denied any history of fever, chills, night sweats, weight loss, or cough.
subjective.review_of_systems: Fatigue, headache. Denies fever, night sweats, cough, or weight loss.

objective.physical_examination: Pallor and clinical icterus. Lymph node examination revealed multiple left cervical lymph nodes that were firm, nontender, matted, and mobile. Abdominal examination demonstrated mild splenomegaly. Remainder of physical examination was unremarkable.
objective.routine_investigations: Hemoglobin 3.5 g/dL, total WBC count 4,800/mm3 (52% neutrophils, 48% lymphocytes), platelet count 225,000/mm3, MCV 97 fL, MCH 30.5 pg (fL), reticulocyte count 12%. Peripheral blood smear showed anisopoikilocytosis with macrocytosis and spherocytosis. Direct Coombs test was positive. Total bilirubin 3.7 mg/dL, direct bilirubin 2.0 mg/dL, indirect bilirubin 1.7 mg/dL, LDH 720 U/L, haptoglobin 20 mg/dL. Serum urea and creatinine within normal limits; glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) activity was normal. Serologic tests for antinuclear antibodies (ANA), HIV, Mycoplasma, hepatitis B virus, and hepatitis C virus were negative. Mantoux tuberculin test was positive with 18 mm induration. Chest X-ray was normal. Abdominal ultrasound revealed splenomegaly.
objective.advanced_workup: Bone marrow examination showed marked erythroid hyperplasia. Excisional biopsy of the left cervical lymph node was performed.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Tuberculous cervical lymphadenitis complicated by warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia (AIHA).
Diagnostic confirmation: Histopathological examination of the left cervical lymph node biopsy demonstrated caseating granulomatous lymphadenitis; Mantoux test strongly positive (18 mm induration); direct Coombs test positive with severe Coombs-positive hemolytic anemia (Hb 3.5 g/dL, reticulocytes 12%, LDH 720 U/L, elevated indirect bilirubin).
Management and outcome: Initiated on 4-drug antituberculosis chemotherapy: isoniazid 300 mg once daily, rifampicin 450 mg once daily, ethambutol 800 mg once daily, and pyrazinamide 750 mg twice daily. Fatigue and headache improved within 2 weeks of therapy; hemoglobin rose to 5.0 g/dL at 2 weeks without hemolysis flare; direct Coombs test converted to negative after 2 months of treatment. Patient remains in excellent health on long-term follow-up.
